scope: Fresh zero-authorship source/component re-verification of picker identity-refusal repair; native browser acceptance is outside this lane.

addressed.finding: Identity refusal routed to generic capture retry
addressed.evidence: useScrape.launchDiagnose now writes diagnose.launchError for the captured tab when page identity is unavailable. ScrapeView renders DiagnoseLauncher during that unresolved interval; its Retry picker calls launchDiagnose, while CaptureErrorCard and captureActiveTab are not used.

addressed.finding: Refusal remedy vanished during temporary identity loss
addressed.evidence: The hook retains the error while the same tab has a null pageKey, and DiagnoseLauncher displays it using the tab ID. The real-hook component test checks the alert after identity loss and rerender.

addressed.finding: Old document or picker session could affect a new page
addressed.evidence: The hook clears the remedy on a different pageKey, rejects a stale Pick control, and checks session ID plus current page identity before applying late picker results or failures. Focused tests exercise these races.

evidence: A Pick click during same-tab identity recovery shows a picker-specific alert and Retry picker, leaves the captured object in the store, and does not call scripting until identity is ready.
Retry picker launches the picker on the restored document, while the original injection-rejection path still exposes a picker-specific retry.
ScrapeView's actual rendering condition keeps DiagnoseLauncher visible for the captured tab during temporary identity loss; the view's generic capture retry remains wired only to CaptureErrorCard.
Different-document identity and stale-session tests leave no old result or remedy on the new page.
limitations: No native Chrome sidepanel interaction, real navigation timing, or visual layout was checked in this lane.
The real-hook component test renders DiagnoseLauncher rather than the complete ScrapeView; full-view visibility is confirmed by source routing.

evidence: The repair uses the existing active-tab identity, scrape store, DiagnoseLauncher, and picker session. It introduces no second picker or capture pathway.
The refusal is visible with an actionable retry, and the retry does not recapture or replace existing user content.

The new test reaches the real hook from a rendered Pick button and asserts capture preservation, no injection during refusal, visible recovery, successful retry, and stale-document rejection. The builder recorded assertion-red before the fix and an executed branch/constant mutation after it.
limitations: I did not independently replay the builder's mutation; I inspected its recorded red/green and reran the focused tests.
